title: Global LR scale x0.75 (all four LR constants)
description: EMBEDDING_LR 0.6->0.45, UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004->0.003, MATRIX_LR 0.04->0.03, SCALAR_LR 0.5->0.375; schedule, HEAD_DIM 128, DEPTH 10, batch 2^18 all untouched.
reflection:
NULL RESULT, and a clean one: val_bpb 0.988598 vs the 0.988076 baseline, +0.00052, inside the 4-7e-4 noise floor. Every other number is a near-exact match to the baseline - 1120 steps vs 1119, 293.6M vs 293.3M tokens, MFU 41.99 vs 41.94, final smoothed train loss 2.7566 vs 2.752 - so this is close to replicate quality and the LR is genuinely the only thing that differed. Cutting EVERY learning rate by 25% changes nothing measurable.

The finding is the shape of the LR basin, not the point estimate. Round 2 measured three up-moves, all losses (Muon +37% -> +0.0056, Muon +50% -> +0.0032, warmdown 0.3 i.e. +10% average lrm -> +0.0056), and the group - me included - read that as 'the run is over-stepped, walk down the gradient'. Wrong inference. The basin is ASYMMETRIC: flat for at least 25% below 0.04, rising above it. The baseline sits at the edge of a plateau, not on a slope, so there is no descent to walk. That also kills the mechanism I argued for in my slot claim - that the round-0 batch halving (2^19 -> 2^18) left the LRs ~sqrt(2) too hot and needed a compensating cut. If that were true a 0.75x cut would have recovered it; it recovered nothing.

Direct consequence for this round's other five arms: all six of us proposed WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.7, which cuts the time-averaged LR multiplier 0.75 -> 0.65, i.e. -13% on the same quantity I just cut by 25% for zero effect. I predict those arms land at ~0.988 +/- noise. If they do, the LR/schedule region is closed on the down side and should not absorb more slots; the remaining LR question is only whether there is a narrow optimum between 0.04 and 0.055, which is not worth a run for a sub-0.003 prize.

What is still untouched after 20 of 36 runs: WINDOW_PATTERN (zero runs all cell), ADAM_BETAS, WEIGHT_DECAY, the MLP ratio, and throughput-at-fixed-math (a2's max-autotune, still unmeasured after the phantom row in r02). With the size box closed on all four sides and the LR basin now shown to be flat below, those are the only regions left with any prior.
